title: Solving word problems by drawing a picture
examples: How do I solve a word problem?
Do I add or take away in a word problem?
How does drawing help with maths?

explain.say: Here is a story with maths inside. Ana has 5 apples. Her gran gives her 3 more. How many apples does she have now? Word problems get easier when you draw them. Look at the board.

draw.text: Solving word problems by drawing a picture

explain.say: Step one: read the story. Step two: draw it. You do not need beautiful apples! Five dots for Ana's apples is perfect. Can you draw five dots?

steps.label: Read it
steps.note: Read the story, or ask a grown-up to read it.

steps.label: Draw it
steps.note: Draw dots or simple shapes for the things.

steps.label: Add or take away?

explain.say: Step three: ask, is it getting more, or fewer? Gran gives Ana more apples, so we add. Draw three more dots. More means add!

steps.label: Read it
steps.note: Read the story, or ask a grown-up to read it.

steps.label: Draw it
steps.note: Draw dots or simple shapes for the things.
steps.ask: Do I need to draw real apples?

steps.label: Add or take away?

explain.say: Step four: count your picture. Five dots and three more: six, seven, eight. Ana has eight apples! Look at the ten frame: five and three make eight.
Try this one. Kenji has 9 stickers. He gives 4 away. Fewer, so take away. Draw nine dots and cross out four. Five are left! Fantastic problem solving! Challenge: make up your own maths story.

faq.q: Do I need to draw real apples?
faq.a: No! Dots, circles or lines are perfect. The picture just helps you see the numbers.

faq.q: How do I know if I add or take away?
faq.a: Ask: is it getting more, or fewer? More, like given or joined, means add. Fewer, like eaten or given away, means take away.

faq.q: What if I cannot read the story?
faq.a: Ask a teacher or grown-up to read it to you. Understanding the story is the important part.
asks: Can someone read the problem to me?

faq.a: A picture turns words into something you can see and count. Then the maths is right there in front of you.

faq.q: How do I check my answer?
faq.a: Count your picture again, and ask: does it make sense in the story? Ana started with 5 and got more, so 8 makes sense.

quiz.say: Ana has 5 apples and gets 3 more. Do you add or take away?
quiz.show: Ana has 5 apples and gets 3 more. Add or take away?
quiz.why: She gets more apples, so you add.

wrong.1: Take away is for when things go. Ana gets more.
wrong.2: The number of apples changes, so you need to add.

quiz.say: Kenji has 9 stickers and gives away 4. How many are left?
quiz.show: 9 stickers, 4 given away. How many left?
quiz.why: Nine take away four is five.

wrong.1: 13 is nine add four. Giving away means take away.
wrong.2: Four is how many he gave away, not how many are left.
